OpenCode With Ollama: Verify Your Local Model

Start Ollama with a downloaded text model, then open /models in OpenCode 2. It discovers completion models at 127.0.0.1:11434 by default. If Ollama listens on another port, set providers.ollama.settings.baseURL to its address ending in /v1, then copy the exact ollama/ model ID from the list.

  1. Check model discovery
  2. Find the failure
  3. Configure a custom port
  4. Verify a local request
  5. See the test results

Check model discovery in OpenCode 2

  1. Run opencode --version. This guide uses V2’s providers configuration. Check the migration guide before using V2 settings in an older installation.
  2. Start Ollama and check that your model exists. If you need a small test model, follow the first local Ollama run.
  3. Open /models in the OpenCode client, or use opencode models --standalone from a disposable project. Look for the exact ollama/ entry, including the model tag.

--standalone starts a private OpenCode server for that command. If you normally use an existing server or Desktop, verify its model list separately. The server process needs to reach Ollama from wherever it is running.

Where does the connection stop?

Ollama answers on a different port

Verify the actual Ollama port with its native API. This example assumes port 11440 and an already running local server:

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS \
  http://127.0.0.1:11440/api/tags

In a disposable test project, save this configuration as opencode.json. If you are applying it to a real project, keep a copy of your configuration and merge the provider entry.

{
  "providers": {
    "ollama": {
      "settings": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1"
      }
    }
  }
}

OpenCode derives Ollama’s native discovery paths from the base URL. Use /v1 in the OpenCode configuration and /api/tags from the host root for the direct check. For this local test, keep Ollama bound to loopback.

Ollama answers but OpenCode shows no model

Check that /api/tags lists the full name you expect. If the model is listed there, query Ollama’s /api/show with that exact name and look for completion in capabilities. OpenCode’s built-in discovery omits embedding-only models. Select a downloaded model that generates text for the check below.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS \
  http://127.0.0.1:11440/api/show \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen-local-first:latest"}'

If the native check works and opencode models --standalone differs from the client picker, confirm that both are using the same workspace and server configuration. A previously successful list can also survive a temporary outage, so verify the running server before relying on the picker.

Verify a request reached Ollama

In a scratch project with no private files, send a short prompt using the exact ID you saw. Replace our imported alias with your own. Before running it, merge this test-only provider body and permission rule into the scratch project’s configuration. Keep the existing settings.baseURL if you use a custom port.

{
  "providers": {
    "ollama": { "body": { "max_tokens": 32, "temperature": 0 } }
  },
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}

The output cap is for this short probe. Keep this example in the scratch project so it does not cap later coding tasks.

opencode run --standalone --agent plan \
  --model ollama/qwen-local-first:latest \
  "Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else."

Check for a reply, then immediately check ollama ps for the same tag. For a custom port, point the Ollama CLI at it first, or query /api/ps on that port. Prefer an otherwise idle test server so you can identify which request loaded the model. A connection test says little about how well it can edit a repository.

If the model is visible but the request fails, read the first error and verify the port again. For memory or context errors, check the actual running setting using the Ollama context guide. Ollama recommends a larger context for OpenCode coding workloads. Use the local test above to establish connectivity before choosing a coding model.

What the controlled port test showed

We tested OpenCode 2.4.1 and Ollama 0.40.18 on Apple Silicon with the same downloaded Qwen GGUF. With a fresh OpenCode profile pointed at an unused port, opencode models --standalone exited with code 0 and did not list our model. A fresh profile pointed at the working port listed ollama/qwen-local-first:latest. Check the model ID in the output even when the listing command exits successfully.

The first, uncapped request reached Ollama but timed out after 55 seconds. After setting the 32-token cap and temperature 0, a fresh run returned LOCAL_OK and stopped normally. Ollama reported no loaded model before the bounded request and the test model at 8,192 context tokens afterward. Both processes were restricted to loopback during the test. This result verifies discovery and a small request with that setup. Download the configurations and filtered results.

Sources checked November 28, 2026. OpenCode’s Ollama provider instructions document discovery and the custom base URL. The Ollama integration guide covers its launcher and coding context recommendations. For broader setup and permission checks, see the OpenCode project guide.
